details: Lisk (LSK) experienced a significant price surge of 269% to $0.89 following announcements of its blockchain shutdown, migration plans, and a proposed 100 million LSK token burn, reducing supply from 400 million to 300 million by October 2026. This move aims to transition Lisk towards an enterprise-focused model. The migration deadline has created urgency, amplified by derivatives trading.
title: Lisk (LSK) Surges 269% on Blockchain Migration and Token Burn Plans

details: Institutional investment flows are diverging, with Bitcoin Spot ETFs experiencing their fourth consecutive day of net outflows on September 11, totaling approximately $13.3 million. In contrast, Ethereum Spot ETFs saw substantial daily inflows of $216 million on the same day, marking their largest single-day haul in September, indicating a rotation of institutional capital.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Outflows While Ethereum ETFs Attract Inflows

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has postponed its decisions on several Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF) applications, including those for XRP, Litecoin, and JitoSOL. This extends the period of regulatory uncertainty for these digital assets and the broader crypto market.
title: SEC Delays Decisions on XRP, Litecoin, and JitoSOL ETFs

details: The Liquid Network was hit by an exploit where approximately 4,000 BTC, valued at around $320 million, was stolen from a federation wallet. Reports indicate that about 3,400 BTC was subsequently returned, but the incident highlights ongoing security vulnerabilities in the digital asset space.
title: Liquid Network Suffers $320M Bitcoin Exploit, Most Funds Recovered

details: Bloomberg Intelligence senior macro strategist Mike McGlone has issued a warning that Bitcoin could fall to as low as $10,000. He attributes this potential significant sell-off to Bitcoin's strong correlation with the S&P 500 and anticipated interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, suggesting Bitcoin has lost its "digital gold" safe haven status.
title: Bloomberg Strategist Warns Bitcoin Could Drop to $10,000

details: The US Senate is slated to hold a procedural vote next week on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. This proposed legislation aims to establish clearer regulatory boundaries for cryptocurrencies, potentially bringing more certainty to exchanges, token issuers, and decentralized finance platforms. Greater clarity could encourage institutional investment.
title: US Senate to Vote on Digital Asset Market Clarity Act Next Week

details: Bitcoin recently confirmed a "golden cross" pattern, where its 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) crossed above its 200-day EMA. This technical indicator is often seen as a bullish signal, suggesting that short-term buying momentum is overcoming longer-term trends. Despite this, Bitcoin is consolidating near $77,000 and has faced resistance breaking above $80,000.
title: Bitcoin Forms "Golden Cross" Amidst Consolidation

details: Circle, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, is reportedly acquiring Singapore-based Tazapay in a deal valued at $400 million. This strategic acquisition is seen as a move to gain local payment rails, licenses, and banking relationships in emerging markets, crucial for expanding the utility of stablecoins in global commerce.
title: Circle's Tazapay Acquisition Bolsters Stablecoin Reach in Emerging Markets

details: The Ethereum Foundation has established a target deadline of December 2029 to make the Ethereum network fully resistant to quantum computing attacks across all its infrastructure layers. This proactive measure aims to safeguard transaction processing, validator security, and data storage against the future threat of quantum computers.
title: Ethereum Foundation Sets 2029 Deadline for Quantum Resistance
